model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; residual income equivalent on book, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total income (net interest income + fee and commission income + other non-interest income, group basis). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported; FY0 = 1H26 actual 12,041 (D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:143) + 2H26E ~11,700 (2H25 was 11,263; 2Q26 run-rate 6,093 x2 = 12,186 less the usual 2H seasonal softening in markets trading). FY2025 actual 22,900. Management guided FY2026 total income 'around 2025 levels' (D05.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt CFO outlook, ~line 840); 1H26 is running +3% YoY, and at the 2Q26 results (Aug 2026) management raised it to 'exceed FY2025 levels' with commercial-book non-interest income growing mid-teens (D05.SI_Analysis.json guidance block), so FY0 at +3.7% is consistent with the raised guide. Using FY2026E as FY0 makes year 1 = FY2027, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,844m issued ordinary shares net of treasury at 30 Jun 2026 (D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1603-1615) plus ~9m potential shares under the DBSH Share Plan (1H26 weighted average 2,850m diluted vs 2,841m basic, :1617) = 2,853m fully diluted. The 2024 1-for-10 bonus issue is already in this count (FY2023 2,578m -> FY2024 2,843m); pre-2024 per-share history is not bonus-adjusted in the CSV. Held FLAT: share-plan cost (~S$225m/yr) is expensed in the flows, and the remaining ~S$2.6bn of the S$3bn buyback programme is captured as the excess-capital equity_bridge item, not as a falling share count (counting both would double-count).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. DBS is a MAS-regulated D-SIB: customer deposits (S$638.2bn), due to banks (S$94.5bn) and other debt securities (S$86.4bn at 30 Jun 2026, D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1343-1348) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and central-bank balances (S$46.1bn) are held against that funding (LCR 142%) and are not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net profit less capital retained to fund RWA growth) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = net profit ~11,600 (1H26 6,009 actual + 2H26E ~5,600; 2H25 was 5,312 pre-CSR) less capital retained ~3,160 (= NPAT x g/ROE at ~4.5% balance-sheet growth and ~16.5% ROE on required equity). Cross-check: FY2025 distributions were dividends 8,151 + buybacks 397 = 8,548 with transitional CET1 flat at 17.0% -- but that included the start of the excess-capital release, so organic FCFE was lower, consistent with ~8.4bn. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based payments so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero: interest income is the bank's operating revenue, not a return on surplus cash.
inputs.sbc_source: Cost of share-based payments S$111m 1H26 vs S$97m 1H25 (D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1478, statement of changes in equity / cash flow add-back); FY2025 S$203m (core_metrics stock_based_comp). FY2026E ~S$225m. Awards settle from new issues or treasury shares; there is no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025: shares repurchased and cancelled S$371m + treasury purchases S$26m (D05.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt:4665-4668). Nil cancellations in 1H26; S$18m treasury purchases for the share plan. ~12% of the S$3bn programme was completed in 2025.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' funds S$70,166m (ex NCI S$51m; no other equity instruments outstanding after the 2025 perpetual redemption) = BVPS S$24.69 at 30 Jun 2026; goodwill and intangibles S$6,290m -> tangible book ~S$63.9bn, ~S$22.40/share. At the current price the stock trades ~3.0x book, ~3.3x tangible book, ~18x FY2026E earnings.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0% SGD cost of equity, single rate across scenarios (scenario risk is carried in the flows, not charged twice in the rate). Built in SGD: 10y SGS ~2.3%, equity risk premium ~5.5%, beta ~1.0 for a D-SIB with 5.8% leverage ratio = 7.8%, +0.2pp for Hong Kong/Greater China and South/Southeast Asia credit exposure. Not comparable to NAB.AX's 9.7% AUD rate, which sits on a ~2pp higher local risk-free rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (S$1.1bn FY2025) are inside operating expenses via the cost-income ratio; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI S$51m is immaterial (0.07% of equity); net profit used is attributable to shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on book, expressed in FCFE form through the component engine, per the dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' and the house bank precedent (NAB.AX, 2016.HK). Owner-FCF/EBIT-based free cash flow is NOT used: statutory operating cash flow swings with deposits and loans (1H26 -7,127, FY2024 +15,341). Engine field mapping: growth_rates = total income growth; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax profit (after expenses, credit allowances and share of associates) PLUS share-based payments, as % of total income, so that the engine's SBC deduction lands exactly on pre-tax profit; da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation is inside expenses); capex_pct_path = capital retained to fund RWA growth at a constant capital ratio = NPAT margin x g / ROE; cash_tax_rate_path = effective tax rate incl. the 15% global minimum tax from FY2025; wacc = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. With retention = g/ROE the Gordon terminal is identically the residual-income P/B of (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) on required book. Excess CET1 above management's 12.5-13.5% operating range is added once via equity_bridge. D05.SI_Analysis.json landed mid-build; its 2Q26 guidance block (FY2026 income above FY2025, NII closing the gap, CTI low-40s, SP 17-20bp, S$8bn capital return on track) confirms the FY0 anchor and was not otherwise used to move drivers. CONSERVATISM NOT CORRECTED: FY2026 Q4 earnings (~S$2.9bn) are neither in the flows (year 1 = FY2027) nor in the June book; worth roughly S$0.7/share after retention.

equity_bridge.item: Excess CET1 above the top of DBS's 12.5-13.5% operating range (fully phased-in basis)
equity_bridge.note: Fully phased-in CET1 14.6% at 30 Jun 2026 (D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:179) on implied fully phased RWA ~S$435bn (CET1 capital 63,516 / 14.6%). (14.6% - 13.5%) x 435bn = ~S$4.8bn, rounded down to 4.7bn. Cross-check: the unexecuted remainder of the S$8bn excess-capital framework is ~S$2.6bn of the S$3bn buyback plus ~S$2.6bn of Capital Return dividends (6 more quarters x S$0.15 x 2,844m) = ~S$5.2bn, i.e. management is returning essentially this surplus. The retention path in the flows then holds capital at the operating target, so this is not counted twice.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.7% diverges by >30% from revenue (9.4%), net income (18.3%) and EPS (16.1%) 5yr CAGRs. Cause: FY2020 is a COVID-trough base (ROE 9.1%) and the 2022-2024 rate cycle lifted NIM from 1.45% to ~2.1%, while book growth was held down by payouts of 75-80% plus the 2024-27 excess-capital return. Book CAGR is the honest compounding rate for a bank distributing most of its earnings; forward revenue growth in the base case (3-5%) sits between the two.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF is not defined for a bank; fcf CAGRs are null by design. EPS 3yr CAGR is depressed by the 2024 1-for-10 bonus issue (FY2023 EPS not restated in the CSV); on a bonus-adjusted basis FY2022->FY2025 EPS CAGR is ~10%, in line with net income. Periods: FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), FY2020->FY2025 (5yr), Metrics.csv.

base.growth_rationale: Total income. FY2027 +4.5%: loans +8% and deposits +11% YoY at 1H26 with NIM down 20bp to 1.88% as Sora/Hibor fell; the rate drag fades once hedges roll and the deposit base reprices, while fees (+20% in 1H26, wealth AUM >S$500bn) keep compounding. 5% mid-cycle (Asian nominal GDP + wealth share gains), tapering to 3.0% by year 10 to match the terminal rate.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax profit + SBC on total income. Normalised PBT margin 57.0% = 100 - cost-income ratio 40.5% (guided 'low-40%'; 1H26 38.6%, FY2025 40.4%) - credit allowances 3.6% of income (guided specific allowances 17-20bp of loans, ~S$850m on S$470bn of loans; FY2025 S$791m incl. GP, 1H26 annualised S$606m) + associates 1.1%; plus SBC 0.9%. Drifts to 56.6% PBT as technology spend and competition for wealth clients absorb some operating leverage. History: FY2023 58.2%, FY2024 58.3%, FY2025 57.2%, 1H26 59.9%; FY2018-19 50-52% at a lower NIM.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to keep CET1 at the operating target as RWA grows with income = NPAT margin (~47.6% of income) x g / ROE on required equity 16.5% = 2.885 x g. At 5% growth 14.4% of income (~30% of NPAT retained, ~70% distributed: DBS's ordinary dividend of S$2.64/yr is ~63% of FY2026E EPS); at 3% terminal growth 8.7% (18% retained). ROE 16.5% sits below the 1H26 reported 17.5% (which is on a book still carrying ~S$4.7bn surplus capital; ex-surplus it is ~18.7%) because lower rates compress NIM through the forecast.
base.tax_rationale: Effective tax 15.8% FY2025 (2,065 / 13,099) and 16.7% 1H26 (1,206 / 7,216) after the 15% global minimum tax took effect in 2025. 17% mature allows for top-up in low-tax jurisdictions.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.0% CoE and 3.0% growth = 20.6x terminal FCFE, equivalent to ~2.7x required book at a 16.5% ROE. Cap of 22x is a ceiling only and does not bind.

bull.growth_rationale: Rates bottom in 2026; hedges and Casa growth stabilise NIM near 1.9%, wealth fees keep growing high-teens as Asia-Gulf and Hong Kong flows continue, and loan growth holds 7-8%.
bull.margin_rationale: PBT margin ~59% (1H26 run-rate 59.9%): CTI holds at ~38.5% via AI-driven productivity, credit costs stay at the benign 13-15bp of 1H26, associates ~1%. Plus SBC 0.9%.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~49.3% x g / ROE 18% = 2.74 x g. Faster growth consumes more capital even at the higher ROE.
bull.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.0% / 3.5% = 23.0x terminal FCFE (~3.1x required book at 18% ROE); 24x cap does not bind.

bear.growth_rationale: Sora and Hibor fall further and NIM compresses toward the 2021 trough (~1.6-1.7%); wealth flows reverse in a risk-off market after the Iran war shock and tariff escalation; income flat in FY2027 then recovers to nominal-GDP growth.
bear.margin_rationale: PBT margin 51.5% = 100 - CTI 43% (negative jaws as income stalls while tech spend continues) - credit cost ~30bp of loans (6.5% of income; Hong Kong/China commercial real estate and trade-exposed SMEs, cf. FY2016-17 at 31-37bp and FY2020 at 3,066) + associates 1%. Plus SBC 0.9%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~42.7% x g / ROE 14% = 3.05 x g. ROE ~14% is the FY2019 pre-rate-cycle level (13.2%) plus some structural fee mix gain.
bear.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.0% / 2.5% = 18.6x terminal FCFE; the 16x cap binds deliberately, i.e. ~1.8x required book on a 14% ROE, the bottom of DBS's 2016-2021 trading range.

scenario_narratives.base: Rate headwind fades through 2027 as hedges and deposit growth offset lower Sora; fees and treasury customer income compound with the Asian wealth franchise; cost-income ~40.5% and credit costs normalise to the guided 17-20bp. ROE settles ~16.5% on required equity, ~70% distributed, and surplus capital is returned on schedule under the S$8bn framework.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM stabilises near 1.9% from 2027, wealth AUM growth continues at high-teens, AI-driven productivity keeps cost-income below 39% and credit costs stay benign. ROE ~18% with 6-7% income growth for five years.
scenario_narratives.bear: A risk-off Asia (Iran war second-order effects, tariffs, Hong Kong/China property) pushes rates and NIM toward 2021 troughs, wealth flows reverse, cost-income rises to 43% and credit costs reach ~30bp. ROE falls to ~14%, and the market re-rates DBS toward its pre-2022 ~1.8x book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 growth default: DBS is a mature, highly capitalised D-SIB whose recent ROE was lifted by a rate cycle that is now unwinding, so the downside (NIM + credit cycle together) is as plausible as the upside (wealth-led fee compounding). Same weighting as the house bank precedent NAB.AX.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding the regulatory capital its growth consumes, discounted at an SGD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow, which is deposit and loan movement, and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. Net profit is the flow; capital retained at g/ROE is the reinvestment; 8.0% is the owner's required return. This is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at ~16.5% ROE and 3% long-run growth the franchise is worth ~2.7x required book, plus the ~S$4.7bn of surplus CET1 being returned. The ~3.0x book the market pays needs either ROE held near the 1H26 17.5-19% through a falling-rate cycle or a cost of equity nearer 7.5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM: every 10bp on ~S$760bn of average interest-bearing assets is ~S$0.76bn of pre-tax income (~3% of income); 1H26 NIM was already down 20bp YoY.
Credit cycle in Hong Kong/China commercial real estate and trade-exposed SMEs (FY2020 allowances were S$3.1bn vs S$0.8bn FY2025).
Basel III output-floor phase-in to 72.5% by 2029: fully phased CET1 14.6% vs transitional 16.6%; a higher MAS operating expectation would shrink the surplus capital bridge.
Cost of equity sensitivity: at 3.0x book the valuation is dominated by the (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) term; 50bp on CoE moves value ~10%.
Wealth-fee cyclicality: 1H26 wealth fees +33% are market-linked and can reverse quickly in a risk-off year.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (D05.SI, SGD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 52.85-79.05.
data_sources.financials: D05.SI_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, SGD millions) and kpis table; 1H26 performance summary (D05.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) for the latest balance sheet, capital adequacy, share count and dividends; FY2025 annual report CFO statement for FY2026 guidance and the S$8bn capital return framework.
data_sources.qualitative: Filings first; D05.SI_Analysis.json (written in parallel, read at the end of the build) for the 2Q26 raised FY2026 guidance and risk framing.
